asks: What is a fork given, and can it push code by itself?
answer: No secrets, and no access to a repository of its own, unless you, or a rule you set, give it more. It reads a private repository only with a secret that only reads, given by a rule you set. It cannot push until you, or a rule you set, allow it. Code leaves a fork through Git, with a push you allowed or when you bring its commits to the computer it was forked from. A fork never has more than its parent.

sets.says: A fork never has more than its parent.
